entry_state: Subsequent methods preserve impairment weights, surrendered lease rights, cost-asset ceilings and tax origins. The onerous-contract example writes down the existing asset before recognizing the remaining unavoidable loss and follows fulfilment, cancellation and changed estimates. Rule selection has now introduced authority requirements and source identities; its ordering and historical-view consequences continue on page 170.
exit_state: Dated authority, scope, facts and elections govern rule selection. Historical US amendments do not establish current Codification admission, and ASBE lease adoption and tax transition have separate dates. Ping An's adoption, later carrying balances and maturity amounts constrain different questions; its dashes and qualified major-contract statement do not establish absent leases. The chapter's matched-case conclusion remains to be read.
findings: The selection order preserves historical reports, adjustment books and source clocks instead of treating label mapping as conversion between standards.
US lease and tax contrasts remain proposed historical readings, with current authority gaps stated. The CECL comparison is explicitly unadmitted.
ASBE Interpretation 16 changes qualifying tax recognition independently of the lease-adoption date and requires comparative-period effects beyond an opening entry.
Ping An's opening asset/liability difference 833 does not identify an equity adjustment; its later maturity total is neither carrying value nor payment history. No new confirmed defect.
